validation.notes: Root cause: migrateSessionsFromAgentRoot encoded the session header cwd with cwd.replace(/^[/\\]/, "").replace(/[/:]/, ...) - the replacement class omitted backslash, so Windows paths kept their backslashes (e.g. C:\Users\Alice\My Project became --C-\Users\Alice-My Project--, a bogus single directory under sessions/). Fixed with a one-token change: the replacement class is now /[/\\:]/g, matching getDefaultSessionDirPath in packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts (strip exactly one leading slash/backslash, then map every slash, backslash and colon to '-'). Regression .prale-eval/regression.mjs loads the real module via .prale-eval/subject.mjs (loadMigrations, real fs/path, temp agentDir inside .prale-eval/.tmp-regression, removed in a finally block) and runs the exported migrateSessionsFromAgentRoot against real files. It asserts exact encoded directory names for POSIX (/home/dev/project -> --home-dev-project--), drive-letter with backslashes (C:\Users\Alice\My Project -> --C--Users-Alice-My Project--), drive-letter with forward slashes, UNC (\\fileserver\share\team -> ---fileserver-share-team--, exactly one leading separator removed), and mixed POSIX/backslash paths, plus that no created directory name retains '\' or ':'. It also asserts byte-for-byte preservation of session contents (multibyte UTF-8, CRLF, trailing records), that invalid headers (malformed JSON, wrong type, missing cwd, empty file, blank first line) and non-.jsonl files stay untouched with no sessions directory created, that an existing destination is never overwritten (source and pre-existing destination bytes both unchanged, existing session dir contents preserved), that repeated runs are idempotent (no new dirs, no duplicates, bytes intact), and that empty/missing agentDirs are safe no-ops. Verified both directions: node --experimental-vm-modules .prale-eval/regression.mjs exits 0 on the repaired tree, and the identical script run against an isolated copy of the original HEAD migrations.ts fails with AssertionError on the drive-letter case (actual --C-\Users\Alice-My Project-- vs expected --C--Users-Alice-My Project--), exit 1. Limitation: node_modules is absent in this workspace and dependencies must not be installed, so tsc/biome/vitest were not run; the regression is the focused validation and exercises the production TypeScript through Node 24 type stripping instead.
